answers.title: Empty-collection boundary reasoning
answers.prompt: A fictional checker receives a collection and a condition and must decide whether every member satisfies that condition. Without writing code, explain what question must be resolved when the collection is empty. Then describe how you would independently justify its behavior for a nonempty collection, including one case that should pass and one that should not. Focus on reasoning and test expectations rather than implementing the checker.
answers.starter: Begin by defining what the checker is claiming about the members of the collection. Consider the zero-member case separately from collections containing one or more members.
rubric: boundary: Identifies an explicit expected behavior for an empty collection and justifies it using the checker's stated meaning rather than an arbitrary exception.
general: Independently explains the checker's behavior on nonempty collections, with sound contrasting examples and a consistent rationale.
